summary: K. Kanapathypillai (1902–1968) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hartley College and at the University of London (~1934–1936), and he taught Alvappillai Veluppillai.

K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned doctorates at the University of Madras under Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja and at SOAS, University of London under John Brough, later serving as Reader In-Charge at Madras and honorary director of the Adyar Library.

K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under Madhukar Anant Mehendale in 1964. She was affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and under Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge (1945–1948), later serving as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1955–1963).

K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who studied at Downing College, Cambridge. He served at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and was President of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).
K. S. Balasubramanian is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served on the Editorial Committee (attested 2001) and later as Director (attested 2026) at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese (b. 1906) worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts as privaat-docent at Leiden University (1948) and special professor at the University of Amsterdam (1960).

K. Srinivasan works in Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

K. T. S. Sarao (b. 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He earned degrees at the University of Delhi and completed a PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman, becoming a professor at Delhi in 1995.

K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) worked in Indology. He studied at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore (~1924–1929), and he taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College, the University of Madras, and the Archaeological Survey of India, where he worked (~1956–1976) before becoming Professor and Head at Madras (1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987) and as Honorary Director of the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and at Visva-Bharati University, where he taught.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Kaie Mochizuki (b. 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served as a professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyo Mitomo. He held an assistant professorship at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaigyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a doctorate at the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann (1900–1907) and later served as professor at Taisho, Toyo, and Kokushikan universities, and principal at Shiba High School.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa and Keio universities. He lectured at Harvard (~1913–1915) and served as dean and first president of Komazawa University (1921; 1925–1934).
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950), was a student of Sogen Omori, and held a post at Sophia University (~1970–1997).
